name: National Taipei University of Technology - Taipei Tech
overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

  • Not recommended for students with a Chinese passport


National Taipei University of Technology - Taipei Tech

Founded in 1912, National Taipei University of Technology, commonly known as Taipei Tech, is a national public technology university that has nearly 13,000 students.


Taipei Tech was ranked 108 in Asia in 2019 by QS world University ranking, and is among the top 10 universities in Taiwan.

"Taipei Tech was founded at its present location in central Taipei in 1912, making it one of the first higher educational institutions in Taiwan. Though it then consisted of only three departments (Woodcraft, Metalworking, and Electrical Engineering), the institute pioneered industrial education in Taiwan. Within six years, mechanical engineering, applied chemistry, and civil engineering were added to the programs offered. Today, there are over thirteen thousand students at Taipei Tech, studying in seventy-nine programs at seven colleges: Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Engineering, Management, Design, Humanities and Social Sciences, and iFIRST (the Innovation of Frontier Institute of Research for Science and Technology). Taipei Tech has since produced some of the most influential entrepreneurs, leaders, educators, and researchers in the science and industrial fields, and is known as the birthplace for future entrepreneurs. The University is also engaged in a number of local and international projects related to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and University Social Responsibility (USR). Through making SDGs and USR the key initiatives of Taipei Tech’s medium- and long-term plans, we aim to be one of the world’s greenest, most inclusive, and socially-aware universities."
administrative:
1. Application dossier (Warning for Chinese passport)

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Fill the online application form (google form)
  • Official transcript of academic records
  • A recommendation letter from teaching team
  • Statement of purpose (please indicate why you choose NTUT to exchange and your interest in the education in Taiwan)
  • Photocopy of the passport details page
  • One passport-size photo


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Visa

Once your acceptance letter has been received, you must begin the procedures for obtaining your visa.

You must apply for the 'Resident Visa' at the nearest Taiwan Overseas Representative Offices or Embassy in France.

http://www.roc-taiwan.org/fr_fr/post/8905.html

Students have mentioned it takes about a month.

On their side, NTUT will notify the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) to assist the process of visa application.

Once you arrive there, and within 30 days, you must obtain a residence permit (ARC). You must provide the university with your proof of residence permit (ARC). For more information, click here.


3. Insurance and Health

While applying for your visa, make sure to plan ahead for medical requirements, as you need multiple doses over several weeks (Japanese encephalitis, rabies, hepatitis).

You must subscribe to the insurance provided by the university according to the regulations for welcoming international students in Taiwan (more information here).


All international students are asked to complete a medical exam upon arrival in Taiwan. This includes in particular:

  • a chest X-ray for tuberculosis
  • a measles test
  • a rubella test

If you have been vaccinated against these last two diseases, you will need to provide a certificate of vaccination. For this exam, you will have to pay the sum of NT $750, or about 20 euros.


We also highly recommend you to purchase an international insurance in France that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.


To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

After holding ARCs for over six months, students are obliged to carry National Health Insurance (NHI). Fee: about about NT$749/month (20€).


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/taiwan

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Taiwan, click here.

Resources given by the university:

  • International Student Handbook
  • Guide for new students - Spring 2024


5. Campus Life (more information here)

There are plenty of events which are for international students like a welcome party or ones which are focusing on local celebrations.

You will also be able to have a buddy who will help you for the administrative process if needed, but also to visit Taipei and/or Taiwan.


Must follow instragram pages:

@ntut.cbg and @ntut_oia

All around the campus you are able to find various sport facilities.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation

Taipei Tech dormitories include different residence halls that are situated on-campus and off-campus (for off-campus accommodation, see below).


The average traveling time from Taipei Tech off-campus dormitory to the campus is approximately 25-35 minutes via Taipei Metro.

Each room is equipped with a telephone, internet service and basic furniture like desk lamp, desk, chair, and wardrobe. The bed is about 192*95cm. Each room has air conditioner (Need to buy the air conditioner card for using the air conditioner - NTD500 (USD 17) per card) Dormitory fees must be paid at the beginning of each semester.

In general, all rooms are quad rooms.


Dormitory cost for Taipei Tech On-Campus Dormitory :

NTD 9,900 (around USD 320) per person for one semester, plus NTD 1,000 deposit, which will be refunded when checking out. Extra fees will be charged for using AC and laundry machines.


Dormitory costs for summer and winter breaks are charged separately. Please ask the dormitory administrator for rates.


Off-campus accommodation

It is difficult to generalize because comfort and location criteria vary and affect rent prices but monthly rent for a room in a shared apartment can go between 12000NT to 15000NT (335-420€) in Taipei. Make sure to ask for a contract in English. When you sign the lease, in addition to the first month's rent, the landlord will generally ask for two months' rent as a deposit. The deposit will be returned in full or deducted based on the condition of the accommodation at the time of departure. As photos are not always reliable, we suggest you not to sign a long-term lease before you arrive in Taiwan and inspect the accommodation in person. You can book an AirBnb or a hotel room two weeks before school to visit studios.


  • Taipei Tech dormitories off-campus

The average traveling time from Taipei Tech off-campus dormitory to the campus is approximately 25-35 minutes via Taipei Metro. The rooms are the same as the ones on-campus (see above).


Dormitory cost for Taipei Tech Nangang Dormitory (Off-campus):

NTD 9,000 (around USD 290) per person for one semester, plus NTD 1,000 deposit, which will be refunded when checking out. Extra fees will be charged for using AC and laundry machines.


Dormitory cost for Taipei Tech Xinbei (Haishan) Dormitory (Off-campus):

NTD 7,850 (around USD 253) per person for one semester, plus NTD 1,000 deposit, which will be refunded when checking out. Extra fees will be charged for using AC and laundry machines.


Dormitory costs for summer and winter breaks are charged separately. Please ask the dormitory administrator for rates.


  • Co-living spaces

You can also go for co-living spaces like Borderless House and Banana Coliving.


  • Private room in an apartment with roommates

There are many active Facebook groups and it is fairly easy finding an apartment, especially if you start looking during the summer (about 1 month/1 month and a half before back to school in September).


  • Private accommodation

You can choose to live in an apartment of your own. Please note that in this case you probably won't have a kitchen in your studio. Some websites include Myroomabroad (English) or 591 (Chinese).

Important notes 

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial overview (4th year at Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: 700-1000€ depending on the company and dates
  • Visa: about 60€
  • Student status fee: 12€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the company and coverage
  • Medical examinations: about 20€
  • NHI after living in Taiwan for over 6 months: 20€/month
  • ARC (within thirty days after your arrival): 30€
  • Deposit for your accommodation
  • Beddings, etc.


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the New Taiwanese Dollar. 1 € = 35.84NTD or TWD (rate October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

Roughly, plan between 10 000 and 15 000NTD (280-420€) a month (excluding rent).


  • Housing: 200-400€
  • Food: 150-250€
  • Transportation
  • about 35€ for a monthly pass (T-pass)
  • between 50cents-1.2€ for a ride depending on the length (Easy Card that you can recharge)
  • free bike rides (U-bike) under 30 minutes, then it is about 50cents every thirty minutes.
  • Phone, internet
  • about 15€/month (but you will probably need to pay for a few months directly so be prepared)
  • companies like Chunghwa Telecom and Far East Stone have stores at the airport
  • about 11€ for internet on campus
  • Leisure: 100-180€

Prices are indicative and may change.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • You need to have cash on hand because in Taiwan most payments are made by cash.
  • Please check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut (no fees with at Cathay United Bank ATMs).
  • Make sure you pack thick clothes, as it is very humid in Taiwan and can be cold during the winter.
  • It rains a lot in Taiwan, make sure you have an umbrella with you at all times. You can wait until you get there to buy one, they're cheap and get stolen easily!
  • For transport, you have: the HSR (equivalent of TGV in France), the TRA (the local, slower trains), buses (can be less reliable), the MRT, and the bikes. It is easy and inexpensive to travel within Taiwan (e.g., Kaohsiung, Taichung, Chiayi, Hualien) and also to fly to nearby countries such as Vietnam, Japan, South Korea, Thailand...
  • Taiwanese people eat out a lot and you have all sorts of options: night markets, local stalls, breakfast restaurants, buffets, convenience stores, Japanese chains, etc.
  • Scams are quite rare in Taiwan: prices are pretty reliable and it is very safe.
